correctness.rationale: For all finite d>=2, b_i>0 and c,q>0, K is nonsingular and T(q) decomposes into 3x3 modal blocks. The exact determinant is z(z²-(1-c²/q)z+b_i²/q). The extremal product and real polynomial-at-radius inequalities prove c²r²+(B²+beta²)r-B²>=0 for every candidate rate r<1; the positive root gives r_*. At q_*=B²/r_*², root bounds for all intermediate p_i hold and the min mode attains r_*. Equality on both extremal necessary bounds proves uniqueness. Exact-rational test (beta,B,c)=(1,3,4) gives (r_*,q_*)=(1/2,36); packaged check.py passed 9456 supplementary assertions. Nonnormal transients and arbitrary matrices are not claimed.

value.rationale: A scalar Schur approximation Q=qI is a concrete low-cost restriction in preconditioning. Minimizing the exact asymptotic spectral radius of the resulting stationary iteration is mathematically intrinsic and needs nontrivial balancing of distinct modal roots, not a single well-conditioned scalar-mode check. The complete all-dimensional formula and unique optimum produce a sharp two-endpoint design rule and a rational benchmark where q=36 improves the factor from 3/5 at q=25 to 1/2. No claim about GMRES rates or finite-step transients is made.
